used_documents.title: Barrett M82
used_documents.text: The Barrett M82 , standardized by the U.S. military as the M107 , is a recoil - operated , semi-automatic anti-materiel sniper system developed by the American Barrett Firearms Manufacturing company . Despite its designation as an anti-materiel rifle , it is used by some armed forces as an anti-personnel system . It is also called the Light Fifty for its . 50 BMG ( 12.7 × 99mm NATO ) chambering and significantly lighter weight compared to previous applications . The weapon is found in two variants , the original M82A1 ( and A3 ) and the bullpup M82A2 . The M82A2 is no longer manufactured , though the XM500 can be seen as its successor .

A.answer: The Barrett M82 and M107 are essentially the same weapon, with the M107 being the standardized version by the U.S. military. The main difference lies in their designations; the M107 is the standardized version of the M82. Both are semi-automatic anti-materiel sniper systems developed by Barrett Firearms Manufacturing. The M107 is known as the "Light Fifty" and is used by some armed forces as an anti-personnel system. The M107 uses a .50 BMG chambering and has features like a Leupold 4.5-14×50 Mark 4 scope.

The Barrett M107 , like previous members of the M82 line , is also referred to as the Barrett `` Light Fifty '' . The designation has in many instances supplanted earlier ones , with the M107 being voted one of 2005 's top 10 military inventions by the U.S. Army .

Then the Army decided on the Barrett M82 , a semi-automatic rifle . In summer 2002 , the M82 finally emerged from its Army trial phase and was approved for `` full materiel release '' , meaning it was officially adopted as the Long Range Sniper Rifle , Caliber . 50 , M107 . The M107 uses a Leupold 4.5 -- 14 × 50 Mark 4 scope . Overwatch

The Barrett M107 is a . 50 caliber , shoulder - fired , semi-automatic sniper rifle . Like its predecessors , the rifle is said to have manageable recoil for a weapon of its size owing to the barrel assembly that itself absorbs force , moving inward toward the receiver against large springs with every shot . Additionally , the weapon 's weight and large muzzle brake also assist in recoil reduction . Various changes were made to the original M82A1 to create the M107 , with new features such as a lengthened accessory rail , rear grip , and monopod socket . Barrett has recently been asked to develop a lightweight version of the M107 under the Anti-Materiel Sniper Rifle Congressional Program , and has already come up with a scheme to build important component parts such as the receiver frame and muzzle brake out of lighter - weight materials .

B.answer: The Barrett M82 was standardized by the U.S. military as the M107 [1405-2050]. Both are semi-automatic anti-materiel sniper systems developed by Barrett Firearms Manufacturing using .50 BMG chambering [1405-2050]. While they share this designation and function, various changes were made to the original M82A1 to create the M107, including a lengthened accessory rail, rear grip, and monopod socket [4650-5501]. The M107 was officially adopted in summer 2002 as the Long Range Sniper Rifle, Caliber .50, M107 [4234-4573] and uses a Leupold 4.5-14x50 Mark 4 scope [4234-4573].
